exposure: Read in full: README.md and docs/{architecture,automations,configuration,dashboard-card,ecl110,how-it-works,setup}.md. By accident: a grep over docs/*.md printed rows of docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md and one line of docs/HANDOVER.md (issue/PR numbers). Also read two passages of RELEASE_NOTES.md (#265 CARD_VERSION, the version-pinning note). RELEASE_NOTES.md is present in this export, so release-history claims could be checked. Production comments and README cite earlier issue ids (#265, #1227, #1335, #942). None of it was used as a list of things to re-find.

coverage.evidence: Walked three readers. HACS to first plan: 3 dead ends. Feature configuration (two-tank, ECL110, capacity tariff): 4 dead ends. Developer running tests: 0 inside these cells; the path hands off to tests/README.md, which is out of cell. Contradictions were measured against the production seam that decides each fact: setup_section.py (real ConfigFlow), entity_counts.py (platform async_setup_entry), field_labels.py (en.json options forms), service_fields.py (registered service schemas).

Headings: md_headings.py, 174 headings, 0 defects. Tables: md_tables.mjs (markdown-it GFM token stream), 9 misrendered lines. Links: md_links.mjs, 119 relative links, 38 anchored, 0 broken. Duplication: md_dupes.mjs, 677 blocks, 0 exact duplicates. Orphans: grep, 0 docs and 0 images. Stale versions: card_version_doc.py plus grep; one stale literal (v6.6.8).

doc_symbols.py resolved 282 code-span identifiers against the package AST; 1 unresolved, a true negative mention. Mechanism spot-checks: quick setup (quick_setup_promise.py), card version and stamp (card_version_doc.py), setup flow, services, module map and HA boundary counts (grep). how-it-works.md from line 700 on was covered only by the automated checks (see unfinished).

unfinished.what: docs/how-it-works.md lines 700-1317 (prices and tariffs, wood, away, learning loops, 'What the tests actually prove') got only the identifier, link, table and heading checks. No paragraph in that range was spot-checked against its code path.

findings.title: configuration.md 'Initial setup' documents the pre-v6.6.5 flow: no finish menu, Tibber token required, 74 entities
findings.claim: The '## Initial setup' section of docs/configuration.md names none of the 3 finish_setup menu entries the real ConfigFlow shows after the two required screens. It says a Tibber token is required although the first screen completes with price_source=entity and no token. It says 74 entities appear although the platforms construct 75.

evidence.contention_note: count metric, contention-immune; other finder seats were running on the box

perturbation.change: In memory, HeatPumpOptimizerConfigFlow.async_step_finish_setup = async_step_temperature, which restores the straight-line wizard the section draws (--perturb)

findings.metric_definition: Finish-menu entries the real flow returns that the section never names, plus 1 if the flow accepts a tokenless first screen while the section calls the token required
findings.phenomenon_property: The initial-setup reference in configuration.md must describe the flow ConfigFlow actually runs: every menu entry and every required field it enforces, plus the entity count the platforms construct.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Rewrite configuration.md's Initial setup intro, flowchart and step 1 table to match setup.md: price source choice (Tibber or price entity), the finish_setup menu with its three entries, and 75 entities. Alternatively, defer the journey to setup.md and keep only field tables here.

reproduction_steps: Run setup_section.py: menu_entries=3, named_in_section=0, first_screen_accepted_without_token=1, doc_claims_token_required=1, stale_facts=4

findings.title: setup.md Quick setup promises buffer storage and two-tank physics that the quick-setup answers cannot produce
findings.claim: docs/setup.md says a Buffer tank 'yes' stores cheap heat and that the wood-tank probes switch the two-tank physics on. With every Quick setup toggle on and both probes set, quick_setup.derive produces a config whose ThermalParameters has buffer_is_store False and two_tank_modelled False. Both need a throttling mixing valve, which Quick setup never asks for and setup.md never mentions.

perturbation.change: Wrap quick_setup.derive in memory to also return mixing_valve_mode='manual' (a throttling mode), the one answer the page never asks (--perturb)

findings.metric_definition: Of setup.md's two Quick setup storage promises, how many the ThermalParameters built from derive(all toggles yes + both wood probes) fails to honour
findings.phenomenon_property: Every behaviour setup.md attributes to a Quick setup answer must hold for the config quick_setup.derive writes from that answer, or the doc must name the extra setting it depends on.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Doc: in setup.md's five-questions table and wood-probe paragraph, state that storage and two-tank physics also need a throttling mixing valve (Heating system and heat storage), and point to the hydronic layout catalog. Code alternative (D4-owned): have Quick setup ask about the valve. The matching en.json data_description is a D4-s2 lead.

null_control.note: The same answers plus a valve set on the Heating system page honour both promises, so the count keys on the missing valve and not on the harness

reproduction_steps: Run: buffer_tank_volume=500.0 mixing_valve_mode=none two_zone=True wood_tank_configured=True layout=no_valve; unhonoured_promises=2

findings.title: dashboard-card.md upgrade troubleshooting says the card version lags the integration; the stamp makes them equal on every release
findings.claim: docs/dashboard-card.md says the console banner's card version moves only when the card file changes, is often lower than the integration version, and should be compared against a card version in the release notes. The example banner is v6.6.8. But stamp.py:main calls rewrite_card_version on every stamp, CARD_VERSION equals VERSION (6.7.1) at baseline, and it tracks the integration on 5 of 5 simulated stamps.

perturbation.change: Replace stamp.rewrite_card_version in memory with the behaviour the doc describes (leave CARD_VERSION alone when the card bytes are otherwise unchanged) (--perturb)

findings.metric_definition: Share of 5 simulated successive stamps, card otherwise untouched, after which the card's CARD_VERSION equals the new integration version
findings.phenomenon_property: User-doc statements about which version the card banner shows must follow what the release stamp writes.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Rewrite the 'If an upgrade seems to change nothing' paragraph: the banner shows the integration version, so compare it with the installed integration version. Drop the stale v6.6.8 and v5.0.0/4.3.0 example, or state that the equality holds since #265.

null_control.note: The live tree already shows equality, without any simulated stamp
